claim: R-spondin1 (Rspo1) has been featured as a Wnt agonist, serving as a potent niche factor for stem cells in many tissues.
source: R-spondin1 (Rspo1) has been featured as a Wnt agonist, serving as a potent niche factor for stem cells in many tissues.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that references established knowledge about Rspo1's role as a Wnt agonist and stem cell niche factor.

claim: Rspo1 promotes estrogen receptor alpha (Esr1) expression in the mouse mammary gland.
source: Here we unveil a novel role of Rspo1 in promoting estrogen receptor alpha (Esr1) expression, hence regulating the output of steroid hormone signaling in the mouse mammary gland.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments throughout the manuscript.

claim: Rspo1's action on Esr1 expression relies on the receptor Lgr4.
source: This action of Rspo1 relies on the receptor Lgr4 and intracellular cAMP-PKA signaling, yet is independent of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
evidence: This claim is supported by knockdown experiments and genetic models showing Lgr4 is required for Rspo1's effect on Esr1.

claim: Rspo1's action on Esr1 expression relies on intracellular cAMP-PKA signaling.
source: This action of Rspo1 relies on the receptor Lgr4 and intracellular cAMP-PKA signaling, yet is independent of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
evidence: This is supported by inhibitor studies showing cAMP and PKA inhibitors block Rspo1's effect on Esr1.

claim: Rspo1's action on Esr1 expression is independent of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
source: This action of Rspo1 relies on the receptor Lgr4 and intracellular cAMP-PKA signaling, yet is independent of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing Wnt activators and inhibitors do not affect Rspo1-induced Esr1 expression.

claim: Luminal cells-specific knockout of Rspo1 results in decreased Esr1 expression.
source: Luminal cells-specific knockout of Rspo1 results in decreased Esr1 expression and reduced mammary side branches.
evidence: This is supported by genetic experiments using Krt8-CreER;Rspo1fl/fl mice showing reduced Esr1 levels.

claim: Luminal cells-specific knockout of Rspo1 results in reduced mammary side branches.
source: Luminal cells-specific knockout of Rspo1 results in decreased Esr1 expression and reduced mammary side branches.
evidence: This is demonstrated by whole-mount carmine staining of Rspo1-cKO mammary glands.

claim: Luminal cells-specific knockout of Wnt4 enhances Esr1 expression.
source: In contrast, luminal cells-specific knockout of Wnt4, while attenuating basal cell Wnt/β-catenin signaling activities, enhances Esr1 expression.
evidence: This is shown by qPCR and Western blot analysis of Wnt4-cKO mammary glands.

claim: Luminal cells-specific knockout of Wnt4 attenuates basal cell Wnt/β-catenin signaling activities.
source: In contrast, luminal cells-specific knockout of Wnt4, while attenuating basal cell Wnt/β-catenin signaling activities, enhances Esr1 expression.
evidence: This is demonstrated by reduced expression of Wnt target genes Axin2 and Lgr5 in basal cells of Wnt4-cKO mice.

claim: Rspo1 acts as a bona fide GPCR activator eliciting intracellular cAMP signaling.
source: Our data reveal a novel Wnt-independent role of Rspo1, in which Rspo1 acts as a bona fide GPCR activator eliciting intracellular cAMP signaling.
evidence: This is supported by direct measurement of cAMP levels in cells treated with Rspo1.

claim: Estrogen and progesterone are the main players in mammary development and the progression of breast cancers.
source: Estrogen and progesterone are the main players in mammary development and the progression of breast cancers (Hilton et al., 2018; Macias and Hinck, 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Both estrogen and progesterone act through their cognate receptors, estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR).
source: Both hormones act through their cognate receptors, estrogen receptor (ER) and progesterone receptor (PR) (Hilton et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: The upstream regulation of ERα (Esr1) expression is much less understood.
source: However, the upstream regulation of ERα (Esr1) expression is much less understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a gap in current knowledge.

claim: The mammary gland is composed of basal and luminal cells, which can be separated by surface expression of CD24 and CD29/CD49f.
source: The mammary gland is composed of basal and luminal cells, which can be separated by surface expression of CD24 and CD29/CD49f (Shackleton et al., 2006; Stingl et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established methodology cited from previous literature.

claim: ER+ or PR+ cells, consisting 30 ~ 50% of luminal cells, can be enriched by surface expression of Sca1.
source: ER+ or PR+ cells, consisting 30 ~ 50% of luminal cells, can be enriched by surface expression of Sca1 (Regan et al., 2012; Shehata et al., 2012; Sleeman et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established methodology cited from previous literature.

claim: Hormones exert their mitogenic effects primarily through induction of local growth factors.
source: Hormones exert their mitogenic effects primarily through induction of local growth factors (Asselin-Labat et al., 2010; Brisken et al., 2000; Cai et al., 2014; Joshi et al., 2010; Rajaram et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: R-spondin1 (Rspo1) has been identified as a hormone-mediated local factor, whose expression is upregulated by estrogen and progesterone.
source: R-spondin1 (Rspo1) has been identified as a hormone-mediated local factor, whose expression is upregulated by estrogen and progesterone (Cai et al., 2020; Cai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: R-spondin protein family (Rspo1-4) have been reported to function as niche factors for adult stem cells in multiple organs.
source: R-spondin protein family (Rspo1-4) have been reported to function as niche factors for adult stem cells in multiple organs (Greicius et al., 2018; Han et al., 2014; Planas-Paz et al., 2016; Sigal et al., 2017)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Rspo1 has been implicated as critical growth factor in many in vitro stem cell expansion systems, including intestine, stomach and liver.
source: and Rspo1 has been implicated as critical growth factor in many in vitro stem cell expansion systems, including intestine, stomach and liver (Barker et al., 2010; Huch et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2005; Sato et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Rspo1, through its interaction with its receptors Lgr4/5/6, enhances Wnt signaling by attenuating the turnover of Wnt receptors.
source: Rspo1, through its interaction with its receptors Lgr4/5/6, enhances Wnt signaling by attenuating the turnover of Wnt receptors (Hao et al., 2012; Koo et al., 2012)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Rspo1 potentiates phosphorylation of the Wnt co-receptor Lrp.
source: and potentiating phosphorylation of the Wnt co-receptor Lrp (Carmon et al., 2011; de Lau et al., 2011; Glinka et al., 2011; Gong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In the mammary gland, Rspo1 synergizes with another niche factor, Wnt4, to promote mammary basal stem cell self-renewal.
source: In the mammary gland, Rspo1 synergizes with another niche factor, Wnt4, to promote mammary basal stem cell self-renewal (Cai et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Rspo1 expression is enhanced in the diestrus phase of the estrous cycle and during pregnancy.
source: In line with the role of Rspo1 in MaSC regulation, Rspo1 expression is enhanced in the diestrus phase of the estrous cycle and during pregnancy (Cai et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Rspo1 expression enhancement in diestrus and pregnancy coincides with the rise of progesterone level and the expansion of basal stem cells.
source: coinciding with the rise of progesterone level and the expansion of basal stem cells (Asselin-Labat et al., 2010; Joshi et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rspo1 expression is enhanced in estrus, a stage with high estrogen signaling activity.
source: Our recent study also reported the enhanced Rspo1 expression in estrus, a stage with high estrogen signaling activity (Cai et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to recent work by the authors.

claim: RSPO1 treatment enriches estrogen receptor activity in cultured luminal cells.
source: Transcriptome and Gene ontology (GO) analysis identified enrichment of various features, including estrogen receptor activity (Figure 1a and b).
evidence: This is supported by RNA-seq and GO analysis data shown in Figure 1a and b.

claim: The expression of ERα signaling target genes, including Pgr, Ctsd1, and Wisp2 are enhanced in the presence of RSPO1.
source: qPCR analysis verified that the expression of ERα signaling target genes, including Pgr (progesterone receptor, PR), Ctsd1 (Cathepsin D1) (Meneses-Morales et al., 2014), and Wisp2 (Zhang et al., 2012b) are enhanced in the presence of RSPO1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: RSPO1 treatment results in the upregulation of ERα targets, Pgr, Ctsd1 and Wisp2 in ER+ luminal cells.
source: RSPO1 treatment resulted in the upregulation of ERα targets, Pgr, Ctsd1 and Wisp2 in ER+ luminal cells, indicating the further activation of ERα signaling (Figure 1d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: The expression of ERα itself (Esr1) is enhanced by RSPO1 treatment.
source: Interestingly, the expression of ERα itself (Esr1) is also enhanced (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: ER- luminal cells did not respond to RSPO1 stimulation.
source: In contrast, ER- luminal cells did not respond to RSPO1 stimulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Estrogen (Estradiol-E2, E2) is one of the few known upstream regulator of Esr1.
source: Estrogen (Estradiol-E2, E2) is one of the few known upstream regulator of Esr1 (Chu et al., 2007; Kanaya et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: RSPO1 elevated the expression of Esr1 and its target Pgr to a level comparable with E2 treatment.
source: We found that in this ER+ luminal cell culture system, RSPO1 elevated the expression of Esr1 and its target Pgr to a level comparable with E2 treatment (compare Figure 1d–e with Figure 1f).
evidence: This is supported by comparing qPCR data in Figure 1d-e with Figure 1f.

claim: The upregulation of ERα protein by RSPO1 was confirmed by Western blot analysis.
source: The upregulation of ERα protein by RSPO1 was confirmed by Western blot analysis (Figure 1g).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: RSPO1 upregulates the expression of Esr1 and ERα signaling targets Pgr and Greb1 in mouse mammary Eph4 cells in a dose-depending manner.
source: This role of RSPO1 was further validated in mouse mammary Eph4 cells. RSPO1 upregulates the expression of Esr1 and ERα signaling targets Pgr and Greb1 (growth regulation by estrogen in breast cancer 1) in a dose-depending manner (Figure 1—figure supplement 2a–c).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2a-c.

claim: RSPO1 can induce luciferase expression driven by the ESR1 promoter in a dose-dependent manner.
source: We found that RSPO1 can induce luciferase expression in a dose-dependent manner, while the control reporter lacking ESR1 promoter was not activated in any conditions (Figure 1h).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 1h.

claim: Rspo1 enhances Esr1 transcription.
source: Together, these data suggest that Rspo1 enhances Esr1 transcription.
evidence: This is an inference based on the luciferase reporter assay results.

claim: All three Lgr receptors, Lgr4/5/6 are expressed in basal cells.
source: qPCR analysis indicated that all three Lgr receptors, Lgr4/5/6 are expressed in basal cells, but only Lgr4 is expressed in luminal cells (Figure 2a)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Only Lgr4 is expressed in luminal cells.
source: qPCR analysis indicated that all three Lgr receptors, Lgr4/5/6 are expressed in basal cells, but only Lgr4 is expressed in luminal cells (Figure 2a)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Rspo1 may rely on Lgr4 to signal in luminal cells in the context of Esr1 induction.
source: suggesting that Rspo1 may rely on Lgr4 to signal in luminal cells in the context of Esr1 induction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression pattern of Lgr receptors.

claim: Lgr4 was evenly distributed in ER+ (Sca1+) and ER- (Sca1-) luminal cells.
source: Within the luminal compartment, Lgr4 was evenly distributed in ER+ (Sca1+) and ER- (Sca1-) luminal cells (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: In situ hybridization validated the expression pattern of Lgr4 in both basal and luminal layers.
source: In situ hybridization validated the expression pattern of Lgr4 in both basal and luminal layers (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by in situ hybridization data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: Lgr4 knockdown suppressed the upregulation of Esr1 induced by RSPO1.
source: Lgr4 knockdown suppressed the upregulation of Esr1 induced by RSPO1 (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: LGR4 knockdown inhibited the luciferase activities induced by RSPO1 in T47D cells.
source: In an ESR1-luciferase reporter assay using T47D (a human breast cancer cell line), LGR4 knockdown also inhibited the luciferase activities induced by RSPO1 (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Rspo1 relies on Lgr4 to activate Esr1 expression.
source: Results suggest that Rspo1 relies on Lgr4 to activate Esr1 expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the knockdown experiments.

claim: Addition of Wnt4 alone was ineffective in activating Esr1 expression in primary luminal cells.
source: Intriguingly, addition of Wnt4 alone was ineffective in activating Esr1 expression in these cells (Figure 3b)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Wnt4+RSPO1 combination was unable to further increase Esr1 level compared to RSPO1 alone.
source: and Wnt4+RSPO1 combination was unable to further increase Esr1 level compared to RSPO1 alone (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: Canonical Wnt signaling may not be involved in Rspo1-mediated Esr1 regulation.
source: These results suggest that canonical Wnt signaling may not be involved in this regulatory axis.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of synergy between Wnt4 and Rspo1 on Esr1 expression.

claim: Wnt-signaling activators markedly increased the expression levels of Axin2.
source: Although Wnt-signaling activators markedly increased the expression levels of its target gene Axin2 (Figure 3c), they could not stimulate Esr1 expression (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Wnt-signaling activators could not stimulate Esr1 expression.
source: Although Wnt-signaling activators markedly increased the expression levels of its target gene Axin2 (Figure 3c), they could not stimulate Esr1 expression (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Wnt3a and CHIR treatment suppressed Esr1 expression.
source: In contrast to their stimulating effect to Axin2, Wnt3a and CHIR treatment suppressed Esr1 expression (Figure 3d)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling represses the expression of luminal differentiation genes, mainly Esr1.
source: an observation in line with a previous report, in which Wnt/β-catenin signaling represses the expression of luminal differentiation genes, mainly Esr1 (Lindley et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Inhibition of the Frizzled receptor using FzCRD or stimulating β-catenin degradation using XAV939 effectively suppressed Axin2 expression induced by Wnt3a.
source: Inhibition of the Frizzled receptor using its soluble CRD domain (FzCRD) (Hsieh et al., 1999) or stimulating β-catenin degradation using XAV939 (Huang et al., 2009) effectively suppressed Axin2 expression induced by Wnt3a (Figure 3c)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: FzCRD and XAV939 could not suppress Esr1 upregulation by Rspo1.
source: still, they could not suppress Esr1 upregulation by Rspo1 (Figure 3d).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Inhibition of WNT signaling did not affect ESR1 promoter activities induced by RSPO1 in HEK293T cells.
source: Consistently, inhibition of WNT signaling did not affect ESR1 promoter activities induced by RSPO1 (Figure 3e and f).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 3e and f.

claim: Rspo1 induces ERα expression independent of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
source: Together, these data suggest that Rspo1 induces ERα expression independent of Wnt/β-catenin signaling.
evidence: This is an inference based on multiple experiments showing Wnt signaling modulators do not affect Rspo1's effect on Esr1.

claim: Whole-mount carmine staining showed significantly reduced side branches in Rspo1-cKO mice when compared with the control.
source: Whole-mount carmine staining showed significantly reduced side branches in Rspo1-cKO mice when compared with the control (Rspo1fl/fl) (Figure 4c and d).
evidence: This is supported by whole-mount imaging and quantification shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: The reduced side branches in Rspo1-cKO mice are consistent with previous observation in a Rspo1-/- mammary transplantation model.
source: These results are consistent with previous observation in a Rspo1-/- mammary transplantation model (Chadi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Rspo1 is predominantly expressed in ER- luminal cells.
source: Of note, Rspo1 is predominantly expressed in ER- luminal cells as described previously (Cai et al., 2014)
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: Esr1 is expressed in ER+ luminal cells.
source: while Esr1 is expressed in ER+ luminal cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Esr1 expression pattern.

claim: Rspo1-Esr1 regulation is likely achieved through a paracrine manner in vivo.
source: Thus, this Rspo1-Esr1 regulation is likely achieved through a paracrine manner in vivo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the different cell populations expressing Rspo1 and Esr1.

claim: Decreased ERα expression was observed in Rspo1-cKO mammary gland by whole-mount immunofluorescence staining.
source: By whole-mount immunofluorescence staining, we observed the decreased ERα expression in Rspo1-cKO mammary gland (Figure 4g).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: Quantification indicated decreased percentage of ERα+ cells in Rspo1-cKO mammary gland.
source: Quantification indicated decreased percentage of ERα+ cells (Figure 4h), likely reflecting the overall reduction of ERα level in luminal compartment.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data shown in Figure 4h.

claim: ERα levels were reduced in ER+ luminal cells of Rspo1-cKO mice as shown by qPCR.
source: We found that ERα levels were reduced in this compartment as shown by qPCR (Figure 4i) and Western analysis (Figure 4j).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4i.

claim: ERα levels were reduced in ER+ luminal cells of Rspo1-cKO mice as shown by Western analysis.
source: We found that ERα levels were reduced in this compartment as shown by qPCR (Figure 4i) and Western analysis (Figure 4j).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4j.

claim: ERα signaling target genes, including Pgr, Wisp2 and Ctsd1 were declined in Rspo1-cKO group.
source: Consistently, ERα signaling target genes, including Pgr, Wisp2 and Ctsd1 were declined in Rspo1-cKO group (Figure 4k).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4k.

claim: Loss of Rspo1 results in reduced ERα expression and its signaling activities in luminal cells.
source: Therefore, together these results suggest that loss of Rspo1 results in reduced ERα expression and its signaling activities in luminal cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined data from Rspo1-cKO mice.

claim: Lgr4lacZ/lacZ mammary glands displayed significantly less side branches at 9 weeks.
source: At 9 weeks, Lgr4lacZ/lacZ mammary glands displayed significantly less side branches (Figure 4—figure supplement 2a–b).
evidence: This is supported by whole-mount imaging and quantification shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2a-b.

claim: Immunostaining revealed decreased ERα expression in Lgr4lacZ/lacZ mammary gland.
source: Immunostaining revealed decreased ERα expression in Lgr4lacZ/lacZ mammary gland (Figure 4—figure supplement 2c–d).
evidence: This is supported by immunostaining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2c-d.

claim: Esr1 was significantly reduced in Lgr4 mutant ER+ luminal cells.
source: When ER+ luminal cells (Lin-, CD24+, CD29lo, Sca1+) were isolated, we found that Esr1 was significantly reduced in Lgr4 mutant, so were the ERα downstream targets Pgr, Ctsd1 and Wisp2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2e).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2e.

claim: ERα downstream targets Pgr, Ctsd1 and Wisp2 were reduced in Lgr4 mutant ER+ luminal cells.
source: When ER+ luminal cells (Lin-, CD24+, CD29lo, Sca1+) were isolated, we found that Esr1 was significantly reduced in Lgr4 mutant, so were the ERα downstream targets Pgr, Ctsd1 and Wisp2 (Figure 4—figure supplement 2e).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2e.

claim: Lgr4 plays a role in mediating Rspo1-induced ERα expression.
source: These results support that Lgr4 plays a role in mediating Rspo1-induced ERα expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Lgr4 mutant phenotype.

claim: Loss of Wnt4 resulted in reduced side branching.
source: Loss of Wnt4 resulted in reduced side branching (Figure 5c and d), consistent with a previous report using MMTV-Cre;Wnt4fl/fl model (Rajaram et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by whole-mount imaging and quantification shown in Figure 5c and d.

claim: The reduced side branching in Wnt4-cKO mice is consistent with a previous report using MMTV-Cre;Wnt4fl/fl model.
source: Loss of Wnt4 resulted in reduced side branching (Figure 5c and d), consistent with a previous report using MMTV-Cre;Wnt4fl/fl model (Rajaram et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Loss of Wnt4 increases ERα level in ER+ luminal cells as shown by qPCR.
source: qPCR and Western analyses both indicated that loss of Wnt4 increases ERα level in ER+ luminal cells (Figure 5f–g)
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5f.

claim: Loss of Wnt4 increases ERα level in ER+ luminal cells as shown by Western analysis.
source: qPCR and Western analyses both indicated that loss of Wnt4 increases ERα level in ER+ luminal cells (Figure 5f–g)
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5g.

claim: Loss of Wnt4 increases ERα signaling activities shown by increased target gene expression.
source: as well as ERα signaling activities showed by increased target gene expression (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5h.

claim: The increased Esr1 level in Wnt4-cKO mice is in contrast to the reduced Esr1 level observed in Rspo1-cKO mice.
source: These were in contrast to the reduced Esr1 level and ERα signaling activity observed in Rspo1-cKO mice (Figure 4i–k).
evidence: This is a comparison between the Wnt4-cKO and Rspo1-cKO phenotypes.

claim: The increased Esr1 level in Wnt4-cKO mice is consistent with the in vitro results that Wnt3a and CHIR treatment suppressed Esr1 expression.
source: These were consistent with the in vitro results that Wnt3a and CHIR treatment suppressed Esr1 expression (Figure 3d)
evidence: This is a comparison between in vivo and in vitro results.

claim: Wnt-controlled transcriptional regulator LBH repress luminal genes, mainly Esr1.
source: and consistent with the previous report, in which Wnt-controlled transcriptional regulator LBH repress luminal genes, mainly Esr1 (Lindley et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Wnt/β-catenin signaling targets Axin2 and Lgr5 were reduced in basal cells of Wnt4-cKO mice.
source: The successful deletion of Wnt4 in cKO group was validated by significantly reduced Wnt4 level in ER+ luminal cells (Figure 5e), as well as reduced expression of Wnt/β-catenin signaling targets Axin2 and Lgr5 in basal cells (Figure 5i).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 5i.

claim: In vivo genetic evidence supports that Esr1 regulation is independent of luminal Wnt4.
source: Together, in vivo genetic evidence supports that Esr1 regulation is independent of luminal Wnt4.
evidence: This is an inference based on the Wnt4-cKO results showing increased Esr1 despite loss of Wnt4.

claim: The cAMP inhibitor Bupivacaine HCl (Bup) effectively suppressed ESR1-luciferase activities induced by RSPO1.
source: Amongst over 250 inhibitors, the cAMP inhibitor Bupivacaine HCl (Bup), effectively suppressed ESR1-luciferase activities induced by RSPO1 (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: H89, an inhibitor of PKA effectively repressed ESR1-luciferase activities induced by RSPO1.
source: Consistently, H89, an inhibitor of PKA effectively repressed ESR1-luciferase activities induced by RSPO1 (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Both Bup and H89 suppressed Esr1 expression stimulated by Rspo1 in primary luminal cell culture.
source: Both inhibitors suppressed Esr1 expression stimulated by Rspo1 as shown by qPCR (Figure 6b), but were ineffective on Axin2 expression (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6b.

claim: Bup and H89 were ineffective on Axin2 expression.
source: Both inhibitors suppressed Esr1 expression stimulated by Rspo1 as shown by qPCR (Figure 6b), but were ineffective on Axin2 expression (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6c.

claim: The cAMP-PKA pathway can be activated by estrogen and ERα.
source: Considering the cAMP-PKA pathway can also be activated by estrogen and ERα (Castoria et al., 2008)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: The ERα inhibitor ICI does not affect ESR1 promoter activities that are induced by RSPO1.
source: We found that the ERα inhibitor ICI (ICI182, 780) does not affect ESR1 promoter activities that are induced by RSPO1 (Figure 6d)
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: Esr1-induction by Rspo1 does not involve ERα.
source: suggesting that Esr1-induction by Rspo1 does not involve ERα.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of effect of ERα inhibitor on Rspo1-induced ESR1 expression.

claim: A CRE was found at the proximal promoter of ESR1 (−991 to −984 bp).
source: A CRE was found at the proximal promoter of ESR1 (−991 to −984 bp).
evidence: This is a bioinformatic finding about the ESR1 promoter sequence.

claim: RSPO1 could not activate the ESR1 promoter-luciferase reporter with CRE mutations.
source: While RSPO1 induced the wild type promoter-luciferase in a dose-dependent manner, it could not activate the reporter with CRE mutations (TGcCAgCA) (Figure 6e)
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: RSPO1-FL and RSPO1 R66A/Q71A were able to activate the ESR1-luciferase activities.
source: RSPO1-FL and RSPO1 R66A/Q71A were able to activate the luciferase activities, but RSPO1-N137Q and RSPO1 F110A/F106A could not (Figure 6f)
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: RSPO1-N137Q and RSPO1 F110A/F106A could not activate the ESR1-luciferase activities.
source: RSPO1-FL and RSPO1 R66A/Q71A were able to activate the luciferase activities, but RSPO1-N137Q and RSPO1 F110A/F106A could not (Figure 6f)
evidence: This is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 6f.

claim: The secretion of Rspo1 and its association to LGR4 are critical for Esr1 transcription.
source: suggesting the secretion of Rspo1 and its association to LGR4 are critical for Esr1 transcription.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential activity of Rspo1 mutants.

claim: A dose dependent increase of cAMP level was observed in relation to increasing RSPO1 stimulation in mammary Eph4 cells.
source: We observed a dose dependent increase of cAMP level in relation to increasing RSPO1 stimulation (Figure 6g).
evidence: This is supported by cAMP measurement data shown in Figure 6g.

claim: Rspo1 signals through cAMP-PKA-CREB axis to promote Esr1 transcription.
source: Together, these results suggest that Rspo1 signals through cAMP-PKA-CREB axis to promote Esr1 transcription (illustrated in Figure 6h).
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined results of inhibitor studies, CRE mutation, and cAMP measurements.

claim: This is the first report of Wnt/β-catenin independent function of Rspo1 in physiological condition.
source: To our best knowledge, this is the first report of Wnt/β-catenin independent function of Rspo1 in physiological condition.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the findings.

claim: Rspo1 has a Wnt/β-catenin independent role in antagonizing colon cancer metastasis, in which LGR5 directly binds to TGFβ receptors for the activation of TGFβ signaling.
source: It adds to previous reported Wnt/β-catenin independent role of Rspo1 in antagonizing colon cancer metastasis, in which LGR5 directly binds to TGFβ receptors for the activation of TGFβ signaling (Zhou et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Class-A LGRs (LGR1, LGR2, LGR3) are known hormone receptors that bind to FSH, LH, and TSH respectively.
source: cAMP is a well-known intracellular mediator of protein hormones including FSH (follicle-stimulating hormone), LH (luteinizing hormone), and TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone), which bind to LGR1, LGR2 and LGR3 respectively (de Lau et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Class-B LGRs, including LRG4-6, are reported to promote phosphorylation of Lrp5/6 and stabilization of β-catenin without the G-protein-coupled cAMP production.
